clue.text: Farmer upset in job-this ground will not thaw

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for a job

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: upset means the letters of farmer are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer, unhappy at work, complains that the ground stays frozen solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FARMER into ERMAFR, and 'in' puts that inside POST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that stays frozen all year round in polar regions never thaws.

clue.text: Ostentation of doctor coming up in twopenny case

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the pair that forms a case

parts.note: two pennies give P and P, which act as a case around the rest

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A showy doctor carries a cheap twopenny case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns MO into OM; two Ps (two pennies) enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is showy display and ceremony, the same thing as ostentation.

clue.text: Frost the ancient mariner was in

definitions.meaning: white frozen dew on grass and trees
Coleridge's poem is The ... of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.definitionFit: Hoar frost is a white coating of ice, and Coleridge's mariner appears in a poem whose title uses the old spelling of rhyme.

clue.text: Bird at cove is wild

indicators.note: is wild signals the letters of at cove running riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird flies about a sheltered cove.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Herd sound louder, perhaps, when stooped?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of herd sound louder could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A herd of cattle bellows louder as they bend down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HERD SOUND LOUDER; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a forward-bent posture and hunched back is described as stooped.

clue.text: Humble membership fee outstanding

parts.note: a sub (subscription) is a membership fee
a debt outstanding is due

explanation.surface: A club secretary humbly notes that a member's fee is still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to bring them down, to overpower or subdue them.

clue.text: Master whaler from Omaha boatyard

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A whaling captain sets out from a boatyard in Omaha.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across omAHA Boatyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Ahab is the obsessive master of the whaling ship Pequod in Moby-Dick.

clue.text: It can prove that blood is thicker than water

definitions.text: It can prove that blood is thicker than water

parts.words: It can prove that blood is thicker than water
parts.note: the proverb about family is read literally: an instrument that measures liquid density would show blood is denser than water

explanation.surface: The old saying that family ties outweigh all others.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument for measuring a liquid's specific gravity could literally show one fluid is denser than another.

clue.text: Beer with head on it causes acidity

indicators.note: on places the second piece after the first, as in a down clue one piece sits on another

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: A pint with a frothy head gives the drinker heartburn.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is an English pale ale; NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness or sourness of taste is acidity.

clue.text: Charm of male boss elephant

parts.note: an umbo is the boss, the raised centre, of a shield
Jumbo was a famous elephant, and the name stands for any elephant

explanation.surface: The male boss elephant has a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not a manager but the knob at the centre of a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbo-jumbo is meaningless ritual or incantation, the sort of words spoken as a magic charm.

clue.text: Gallery opening

definitions.meaning: a horizontal passage into a mine

explanation.definitionFit: A mine's horizontal access tunnel serves both as a passage and as an entrance.

clue.text: Firmly impress point of toolbox for example

definitions.meaning: to drive a point home forcefully
a toolbox is where a hammer is kept, its home

explanation.surface: A carpenter makes his point with the sharp end of a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To force an argument across emphatically; and a box of tools is the place where the claw-headed tool lives.

clue.text: Droopy condition of firs in disasters, say

indicators.note: in places the conifers inside the word for failures

parts.note: flops are failures or disasters
firs, say, are pines: conifers in general

explanation.surface: Fir trees wilting in a series of disasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks firs as standing for conifers in general, PINES; 'in' puts them inside FLOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpness, a tendency to hang loosely, is a droopy condition.

clue.text: Cautious with high explosive incorrectly flued

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters of flued are set down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A careful worker handles explosives in a badly built chimney flue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' rearranges FLUED into EDFUL, placed after HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying attention and taking care, one is wary or careful.

clue.text: Former holiness of bad actor around bathing beach

indicators.note: around means the actor's word wraps the beach's word

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, bad actor
a lido is a public bathing place or beach

explanation.surface: A hammy actor once considered holy lounges around the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Halidom is an archaic word for holiness or a holy place, hence former.

clue.text: Swiss water-grass

definitions.meaning: another name for alfalfa, a fodder plant

explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss lake shares its name with alfalfa, a clover-like fodder crop.

clue.text: A working sum at sea

parts.note: a float is a sum of cash kept for giving change, a working sum

explanation.surface: A ship's purser counts a sum while sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: A float is the small amount of money kept in a till to make change.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea means being on the water, buoyant on a ship.

clue.text: Market community?

parts.note: the old Common Market was also called the ... Community

explanation.surface: A question about a town's market traders.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent's union was once known as the Common Market and the European Community.

clue.text: Devilish Lethe mishap open to translation

indicators.note: open to translation says the letters may be rendered in another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A mishap on the river of forgetfulness, the Lethe, open to interpretation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the demon of the Faust legend, so like him means fiendish.

clue.text: Blood factor in outsize wild beasts

parts.note: Rh is the rhesus factor in blood
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A blood test is carried out on large wild animals.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the size label for outsize clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick-skinned horned animals of Africa and Asia are large wild creatures.

clue.text: As salty as aliens out of control

indicators.note: out of control says the letters of aliens run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Aliens running amok in a briny sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' rearranges ALIENS; 'As' and 'as' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Containing dissolved salt is what makes something briny.

clue.text: Guardian spirits behind the scenes

definitions.meaning: theatrical backers who finance a show

explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly protectors, and the investors who finance a theatre production unseen.

clue.text: Carrying no stress, but needing a pick-me-up paradoxically

parts.note: a tonic is a pick-me-up, a restorative drink

explanation.surface: Someone without stress still feels they need a restorative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paradoxically' marks that something unstressed should need a tonic; 'but needing' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, an unaccented syllable carries no emphasis.

clue.text: Official command of guy with appointment

parts.note: a guy is a man
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: A man with an appointment is given an official order.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authoritative order or instruction.

clue.text: Nothing to write about in golf tournament

parts.note: O, shaped like zero, means nothing
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Nothing worth writing home about happened at the golf event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link: the pieces go side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open Championship is a major golf tournament, often just called the Open.

clue.text: One short of ordinary design

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: plain means ordinary
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ordinary design lacking one thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or drawing, a design.

clue.text: Classic trees

definitions.meaning: one of the five English Classic horse races

explanation.definitionFit: A Classic flat race at Epsom, and acorn-bearing trees.

clue.text: Ceylon grass thrown into cellar

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters of into cellar are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Grass from Ceylon is tossed into a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges INTO CELLAR; the definition is 'Ceylon grass'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant grass grown in Sri Lanka, formerly Ceylon, yields an insect-repellent oil.

clue.text: Direction of Tom Brown's chum

definitions.meaning: in Tom Brown's Schooldays, Tom's best friend at Rugby School is called ...

explanation.definitionFit: A compass point, and Tom's friend in Thomas Hughes's Victorian school novel.

clue.text: Man's first to finish odd antics of beggars

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of man's

parts.note: an end is a finish

indicators.note: odd signals the letters of antics put in a peculiar order

explanation.surface: A man is the first to give up the strange antics of beggars.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicants are people who live by begging, such as friars of begging orders.
